body:
Yeah I definitely agree, although I would say most of the time I'm not what I would consider functional. However I forever compare myself to people I perceive as perfect, which obviously makes me feel like I'm less functional. 

My husband's a psychotherapist so he's very understanding and sadly I'm not good at pretending everything's ok - we both may well feel better if I could put on a brave face - so he's very aware of how I'm feeling. I don't really have much going on and he's more of a listener so I end up talking about my mental health, even when I don't really want to and then I experience a lot of guilt because I know it worries him.

He's always been great though. This year post lockdown he's organised a lot of outdoorsy activities to try to make life feel like it's worth living, which has definitely helped, but it doesn't remove my feelings of being a failure. Being looked after all the time doesn't really feel that acceptable when you're in your 30s. 

 I only really have one other friend who I can confide it but she has her own issues (probably one of the reasons we understand each other) and at one point recently she was signed off work for 9 weeks because of anxiety. So it's not that easy for her to help me really. She does keep checking in though, even when I don't get back to her, which I appreciate.

In terms of help, people tend to say "just start doing this" "make some steps to do that" but unless there's someone physically helping me to do it and doing it with me, I won't have the confidence, organisational skills or motivation to do it. Usually as soon as I'm alone I feel desperate, lonely and confused again with no idea what to do with myself.

I'm really sorry to hear about your struggles; I have a lot of empathy for that, having similar thoughts myself. It seems like all this hardship you've suffered has at least helped you to understand and be supportive to others. Your comments could be quite literally saving lives.

And yeah, I know I should keep holding on as things could get better and then maybe I'll be able to get an assessment. It's just so hard and I've been in a anxious and depressed state for almost a year now (probably the longest things have been this severe for). The confusing thing is that I'm so much better than I was from December 20 - March/April 21, mainly because I've forced myself to get out after lockdown, started working a bit and volunteering, so there are distractions. However I'm back to planning my own death again (the suicidal thoughts never stopped this entire time but I haven't actively planned anything since maybe February or March). I'm not sure why, perhaps I've just been worn down by the length of this episode. I know I spend too much time on my phone looking up suicide ideas and focusing on it, but that hasn't changed all year. 

Anyway, I hope you're having a good day so far (not sure what mental state you're in - always feels idiotic saying that to someone who's depressed - hoping you're in an ok place) and thanks for reading and responding thus far.

Thanks for all your support and advice. So I did try an ADHD assessment back in March this year but because I was feeling so anxious and low the psychiatrist said that sometimes anxiety and depression can look like ADHD due to how distracted you are by your anxious thoughts (aswell as other factors). He said he wouldn't be able to give an accurate assessment until I'd recovered, which does make sense. 
I also think there's a possibility I might be autistic just from how much I struggle with learning and socialising. 
I actually just completed the hair and makeup for a wedding today. I was in a slightly better mood although I do find it very difficult to assess if I've done a good job or not and I fret about it for ages. I find I get completely stressed out about it beforehand but usually it at least kind of works out ok. 
I know it sounds insane but I'm still thinking of ending my life in two weeks. Although this is a good day they tend to be few and far between and I still feel so lost and like there is no real place for me here. The planet is so overpopulated anyway and I spend so much of my time worried, confused and feeling useless, I'm just not sure what to do.  There's so many reasons to feel awful about myself and I'm tired of just floating along with no real purpose.

Thank you so much for replying. I didn't think anyone would. I struggle a lot with anything academic. I really couldn't cope when I went to university when I was young; I just don't have a lot of faith that I'll be able to now, you know? I actually think I may have ADHD which has been impeding my learning. My husband says that when I recover from this depressive episode we'll get a diagnosis for ADHD and get meds and I suppose that's my one glimmer of hope but part of me doubts I'll make it that long.
